title: Which feature ships next
goal: Pick the one feature to build next quarter that does the most for customers and the business, without breaking a promise already made.

incident.summary: A six-person product team can build one feature next quarter. Five candidates are on the table. Some of the largest customers have asked for single sign-on, and nobody has looked at cancellations yet.

options.name: Single sign-on
options.description: Let enterprise customers log in through Okta, Azure AD or Google Workspace. Estimated at about 5 weeks.

options.name: Guided setup for new accounts
options.description: A step-by-step setup flow that walks a new small account through its first project. Estimated at about 7 weeks.

options.name: One-click data export
options.description: Let any customer export all of their data to a spreadsheet in one click. Estimated at about 2 weeks.

options.name: Mobile app
options.description: A first iOS and Android app with read-only dashboards. Estimated at about 10 weeks.

options.name: AI weekly summaries
options.description: An automatic weekly email that summarizes each account's activity with an AI model. Estimated at about 3 weeks.

criteria.name: Customer value
criteria.question: How much would building the option help current customers with problems they actually have?
levels: Little or no real help to current customers
Helps a few customers a little
Solves a top problem for most customers

criteria.name: Revenue impact
criteria.question: How much is building the option likely to protect or grow revenue in the next two quarters?
levels: A large, direct effect, such as signed deals or fewer cancellations

criteria.name: Fits the quarter
criteria.question: How comfortably does the option fit into one quarter for a six-person team?
levels: Will not fit into one quarter
Tight, likely to slip past the quarter
Fits easily with time to spare

criteria.name: Evidence
criteria.question: How strong is the evidence in the timeline that customers or buyers want the option?
levels: Some evidence that people want it
Strong, direct evidence that people want it

constraints.name: Can actually ship this quarter
constraints.question: Is there a statement in the timeline saying that the option cannot ship next quarter, for example because a required review or dependency will not be ready?

updates.title: Cancellation analysis
updates.text: Analytics: 6 in 10 small accounts that cancelled last quarter never finished setting up. Support says "how do I get started" is the most common ticket.

updates.title: Sales update
updates.text: Sales: two enterprise prospects, worth about $400k a year together, have put in writing that single sign-on is the only thing blocking their contracts this quarter.

updates.title: Engineering estimate
updates.text: Engineering re-estimated single sign-on at about 7 weeks, because part of the login service needs a rewrite first. The other estimates did not change.

updates.title: Security review
updates.text: Security: any feature that sends customer data to an outside AI model needs a privacy review, and the next review slot is two quarters away.

updates.title: Customer advisory board
updates.text: At the customer advisory board, 7 of 9 customers named one-click data export as their top request, mostly so they can build their own reports.
